name: DatePicker
description: A set of three date picker components built on top of Calendar and Popover. DatePicker selects a single date (controlled via value/onChange or uncontrolled via defaultValue). DateRangePicker selects a date range with a pending state — the selection is not committed until the user presses Aplicar; Limpiar clears the pending selection. DateTimePicker combines a calendar and a native time input in one popover with a pending state confirmed via Aplicar, preserving the time when the day changes. All pickers support locale (es/en), custom date-fns format tokens, date restrictions (fromDate/toDate), and caption layout for navigation. For time-only selection, use the standalone TimePicker component.

components.name: DatePicker

components.name: DateTimePicker
components.description: Combined date and time picker. The user selects a day in the calendar, adjusts the time with the native time input, and confirms with Aplicar. The time is preserved when changing day. Nothing is committed to onChange until Aplicar is pressed. For time-only selection use the standalone TimePicker component.

accessibility.role: The trigger is a Button (role=button). The popover uses Radix UI Popover which manages focus trapping and aria-expanded/aria-controls automatically. The calendar inside uses react-day-picker's table-based structure with proper ARIA semantics.
accessibility.keyboard: Enter/Space opens the popover. Arrow keys navigate days in the calendar. Escape closes the popover. Tab moves between the calendar, time input, and action buttons inside DateTimePicker.
accessibility.aria: The trigger button communicates selected state via its visible text content. Disabled dates receive aria-disabled. The Popover sets aria-expanded and manages focus return on close.

do: Wrap the picker in a container that defines the width — the component stretches to fill its parent. Example:
Use captionLayout="dropdown" when selecting dates far from today (e.g. birth dates, historical records).
Use DateRangePicker for period filters — the Apply/Clear pattern prevents accidental range changes.
Import the DateRange type from the design system: import type { DateRange } from "@traxion-global/design-system/react"
Use dateFormat with date-fns tokens to match your regional format (e.g. "dd/MM/yyyy" for Latin America).
Use date-fns format() instead of toLocaleDateString() when displaying selected dates in your app.
dont: Do not set a fixed width on the picker directly — control width from the parent container.
Do not use DateTimePicker when only a date is needed — use DatePicker to keep the UX simpler.
Do not use DateTimePicker when only a time is needed — use the standalone TimePicker component instead.
Do not install react-day-picker as a direct dependency in your app — DateRange is re-exported from the design system.
